# Caddy — root-to-custom-context

Proxy at /, app on /app context. `rewrite * /app{uri}` adds the prefix on the way in and header_down strips it from Location and Set-Cookie on the way out. The cookie rule is anchored on the end of the header value because Tomcat writes Path=/app with no trailing slash.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/templates/add-prefix.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# Proxy at /, app on the /app context. The public URL stays at the root and the
# proxy adds the prefix when forwarding, then takes it back out of the two
# response headers that carry it.
#
# Compare traefik/http/root-to-custom-context, which cannot touch a response and
# has to arrange all of this on the way in (X-Forwarded-Prefix + FRAMEWORK +
# SERVER_SERVLET_SESSION_COOKIE_PATH). Here the backend needs nothing beyond its
# context path, the same split the Apache, NGINX and HAProxy siblings have.
:80 {
	import common

	# {uri} is the path and the query string, so the query survives the rewrite.
	rewrite * /app{uri}

	reverse_proxy vaadin:8080 {
		header_down Location ^(https?://[^/]+)?/app(/.*)$ $1$2
		# Tomcat writes `Path=/app`, with no trailing slash, so the rule is
		# anchored on the end of the value. One anchored on `/app/` matches
		# nothing, and the browser at / silently stops sending the session
		# cookie back.
		header_down Set-Cookie ^(.*;\s*[Pp]ath=)/app(;.*)?$ $1/$2
	}
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
